channel.title: Artificial Intelligence
channel.description: Official Machine Learning Blog of Amazon Web Services

item.title: Deploy frontier AI models on AWS Trainium with SGLang-Neuron
item.description: SGLang-Neuron is now publicly available through an AWS Deep Learning Container. With SGLang-Neuron, you can serve models and generate reinforcement learning rollouts with SGLang on AWS Trainium using the same SGLang interface you already know, all running on native PyTorch.

item.title: How Natera designed an agentic AI system for lab ops with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: Natera built SWARM, an agentic AI system on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore that captures institutional lab-operations knowledge and deploys it at scale. This post walks through the full architecture, from knowledge base construction to deployment and evaluation, delivering about 130x faster first response and 96.2% automated coverage across support tickets.

item.title: Four Amazon Bedrock inference choices that affect cost
item.description: Your Amazon Bedrock inference bill can keep climbing even after you tune prompts and application logic. Four request-level choices (cache duration, service tier, reasoning effort, and maxTokens) change how many tokens the service processes and the rate applied. We show how we tested each and how to verify the effect.

item.title: Tokenomics at scale: Track and cap Amazon Bedrock spend per IAM principal with CUR 2.0 and AWS Budgets
item.description: Get per-identity Amazon Bedrock cost visibility and enforceable spend limits using only AWS-native features, with no application code for the common case. Attribute spend with IAM principal tags, report with CUR 2.0 or Cost Explorer, and enforce with AWS Budgets actions that apply a Deny policy when a threshold is crossed.

item.title: Optimizing cost per task and proving agent ROI on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: Comparing per-token prices hides the real cost of running a model on Amazon Bedrock. This post shows how to calculate the true cost per task across four hidden cost drivers, reduce it with caching, routing, and output constraints, and prove agent ROI with human baselines, holdout experiments, and a five-dimension scorecard.

item.title: Building a self-service LLM gateway with Amazon Bedrock and LiteLLM
item.description: Build a self-service LLM gateway with LiteLLM on AWS Fargate that puts Amazon Bedrock foundation models behind an OpenAI-compatible API. Developers get instant access through a single API key, while platform teams gain per-user cost controls, quota isolation, and observability.

item.title: Run agents securely and efficiently with the next generation AgentCore runtime
item.description: AI agents now run multi-step workloads for hours and act on behalf of users, raising the bar for secure, scalable agent compute. Learn how the next generation of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime delivers hardware-isolated sessions with faster starts, more compute, usage-based billing, and isolation that now extends to your data.

item.title: Migrate to Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base with your coding agent
item.description: The migration guide in the amazon-bedrock skill helps you migrate a customer-managed Amazon Bedrock knowledge base to a Managed Knowledge Base. Your coding agent plans the move with read-only discovery, creates the new knowledge base or an infrastructure-as-code template alongside the original, and validates retrieval before you cut over.

item.title: Build composable, interoperable multi-agent systems with A2A on AWS
item.description: Build a composable, interoperable multi-agent system on AWS with the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol. A LangChain orchestrator on Amazon ECS communicates with a Strands agent on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore across organizational boundaries, using bidirectional, OAuth-authenticated calls, with neither side depending on the other's framework or SDK.

item.title: Fine-grained access control for Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base tools
item.description: Learn how to expose an Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base to AI agents as MCP tools through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway while keeping per-user access control. A request interceptor injects verified identity, Policy in AgentCore validates it independently, and a resource-based policy restricts direct access to the knowledge base.

item.title: From prototype to production: Engineering agents with Agent DLC
item.description: Agents stall between demo and release when teams lack a repeatable way to measure how good an agent is and whether the last change helped. This post covers three agent properties that break traditional CI/CD, a measured case where an aggregate metric hides a coverage gap, and Agent DLC: one lifecycle, two loops, and one explicit standard for judging every change.

item.title: Build autonomous AI agents with Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI
item.description: Learn how Java developers can build production-ready autonomous AI agents using Amazon Bedrock and Spring AI. This post walks through tool calling, conversation memory, resilience patterns, and multi-agent orchestration, then deploys the agent to AWS with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

item.title: OpenAI Codex on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: A practical guide for enterprises rolling out OpenAI Codex to developers on AWS, with Amazon Bedrock as the model backend, covering the access, governance, and cost decisions that platform, security, and finance teams need to align on.

item.title: Semantic diffing of formal policies with anti-unification
item.description: A textual diff of two formal policies flags every cosmetic change and hides the one that alters behavior. This post shows how to compute a symbolic, deterministic semantic diff with an open-source anti-unification engine, so reviewers see only the genuine disagreements between two candidate authorization policies.

item.title: Detecting and recovering from silent data corruption on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod
item.description: Silent data corruption is a GPU fault that returns wrong but plausible numbers with no error, quietly poisoning distributed training. This post adds three checks to a PyTorch DDP loop to detect it, localize the faulty node on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod, and hand the node to automatic recovery for replacement.

item.title: Introducing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
item.description: Today we're announcing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: your own code can search the web with a single signed API call, with no gateway and no resources to create. Call it from the AWS SDKs or the AWS CLI and use it in applications, agent loops, and data pipelines.

item.title: ICYMI: What landed for AI builders in October 2026
item.description: A recap of the major Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Strands updates from October 2026: new models to match each task, updates that keep agents available and grounded, and clearer cost reporting for AI builders.

item.title: The attendee’s guide to the AWS re:Invent 2026 AI/ML track
item.description: AWS re:Invent 2026 includes more than 140 AI/ML track sessions. This attendee's guide helps you find the breakouts, chalk talks, workshops, and builders' sessions that fit your role and goals, spanning AI chips, models and inference, agents, agent trust, and sustainability, so you can build a smarter re:Invent schedule.

item.title: Automating AWS Agent Registry updates with push-based architecture
item.description: This post shows how to keep the AWS Agent Registry current automatically. Using AWS CloudTrail, Amazon EventBridge, AWS Lambda, and AgentCore Identity, an event-driven pipeline detects MCP server changes and pushes updated tool metadata to the registry with no stored secrets, across single- and multi-account environments.

item.title: How DXC Technology built a multi-model AI substrate on Amazon Bedrock
item.description: DXC Technology runs mission-critical managed IT services for regulated organizations across 70 countries. Learn how DXC built DCX OASIS, its Human+AI operating model, on a governed multi-model substrate in Amazon Bedrock, separating a resilient model substrate from a trusted harness that orchestrates, governs, and audits AI agents at scale.
